S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
examples: Appears not to be listening, looking elsewhere or spacing out during conversation.
Immediately asks to repeat what was just said or instructed.
Does not respond when name is called or answers only after a long delay.
Misses the content of the conversation, giving unrelated answers or out-of-context reactions.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
examples: Frequently loses school supplies or office supplies like pens, erasers, and calculators.
Always searching for glasses, cell phones, wallets, or keys because they do not know where they are.
Loses necessary documents or materials at home or in the office and cannot find them.
Cannot remember where they placed an item they were holding just moments ago.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Inattentive Presentation is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized chiefly by persistent inattention, disorganization, distractibility, losing needed items, and careless errors, with fewer prominent hyperactive-impulsive symptoms though adults may report inner restlessness or difficulty relaxing quietly. It typically becomes clinically evident when environmental demands exceed a person's compensatory routines, and it is distinguished from mood, anxiety, substance-related, or neurocognitive disorders by its persistent cross-situational pattern and functional impairment rather than episodic change alone.

patient.stressor: Yoriel fractured her dominant wrist in a fall at a job site, forcing her away from hands-on carpentry for several months and into estimating, scheduling, permit paperwork, and supervising apprentices from the shop. During the following 1 year and 1 month, without the structure of physical joinery and blueprint-to-build routines, her longstanding tendency toward scattered paperwork intensified into repeated measurement and order-entry mistakes, lost tools and forms, poor sequencing of jobs, and frequent missed information when clients or inspectors spoke to her directly. She became easily diverted by shop noise or competing errands, felt restless when she had to sit through administrative tasks, and had trouble keeping quiet leisure time at home or church, creating real financial strain through delayed commissions and rework. She entered psychiatric care after her occupational medicine clinician and a trusted parish friend both encouraged an evaluation when the recovery had healed but the work impairment continued.

S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
S001.manifestation: I keep putting the wrong measurements or part numbers on estimates, like writing 36 instead of 63 or missing a line on the permit form, and then I only catch it after the lumber is ordered or somebody has to redo the work.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
S003.manifestation: When a client or inspector is talking right to me, I’ll be looking at them and nodding, but then I realize I missed half of what they said and have to ask them to go over it again like I wasn’t even there.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
S005.manifestation: Since I’ve been stuck doing the shop paperwork, I can’t seem to figure out what needs doing first, so bids, schedules, invoices, and apprentice questions all pile up on my bench until I’m rushing and still missing deadlines.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
S007.manifestation: I’m constantly hunting for my keys, tape measure, phone, order sheets, or the notes I just had in my hand, and it eats up so much of the day that the guys have started checking behind me.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
S008.manifestation: What brings me in is I cannot keep my mind on one thing anymore—one saw starting up, somebody walking past the office, or even a thought about another job will pull me off what I’m doing, and then the whole day gets away from me.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: If I have to sit at the desk doing estimates or sit through a long meeting, I feel wound up inside like I need to get up and move around, even though my wrist is healed and I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: Even at home or in church, when things are supposed to be quiet, I catch myself tapping, shifting around, whispering to my husband, or getting up for no real reason because sitting still in the quiet feels almost unbearable.

add_requirements.Onset prior to age 12 years: Even back in grade school, before I was 12, teachers were always telling my mother I was bright but careless, losing homework, forgetting instructions, and staring out the window instead of finishing my seatwork.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: My mistakes and delays have cost me commissions, caused rework on jobs, and made the crew less willing to rely on me for scheduling or ordering. At home, my husband has had to take over bills and reminders because I keep misplacing papers or missing what needs to be done.
add_requirements.duration: This level of trouble has been going on for about a year and a month, since I broke my wrist and got shifted into shop paperwork and supervising instead of hands-on carpentry.
